steps.name: form

steps.name: E

title: Continuity-corrected z-value for a lower binomial tail
source: S2 Ch1 theory S2-1.1 Quick check 3 (B(80,0.4) approximated, z for P(X<=24) is -1.71 to 3 s.f.)
stem: \(X\sim\mathrm{B}({n|int},\,{p|raw})\) is approximated by a normal distribution. Using a continuity correction, find the standardised \(z\)-value used to approximate \(\mathrm{P}(X\leqslant {x|int})\), correct to 3 significant figures.

steps.name: form
steps.text_tex: The approximating normal has mean \({mu|raw}\) and variance \({npq|raw}\). With a continuity correction, \(z=\dfrac{{{num|raw}}}{{{sd|raw}}}\).
steps.note: Standardise with a continuity correction for a less-than-or-equal tail.

title: One-tailed binomial test of a train company's 92% claim

source.note: Stem verbatim from the QP PDF. Steps and marks from the official MS PDF. The item is a one-tailed binomial test at the 5% level, with an assumption and a contextual conclusion; it does not ask for a two-tailed test or for Type I/II errors. Fully manual, steps only, because hypotheses, the assumption and the conclusion are verbal. Official tail P(X<=16)=0.0706 was independently confirmed. A normal-approximation route is allowed in the official scheme after the first two B marks.

stem: A train company claims that 92% of trains on a particular line arrive on time. Sanjeep suspects that the true percentage is less than 92%. He chooses a random sample of 20 trains on this line and finds that exactly 16 of them arrive on time. Making an assumption that should be stated, test at the 5% significance level whether Sanjeep's suspicion is justified.

steps.name: assump
steps.text_tex: State an assumption in context: the trains are independent, or the probability of a train being on time is constant.
steps.note: MS: B1 Assume trains are independent OR probability of being on time is constant. Must be in context.

steps.name: hyp
steps.text_tex: State both hypotheses: H0: P(on time) = 0.92 and H1: P(on time) < 0.92. The letter p or pi may be used.
steps.note: MS: B1 Both. Allow p or pi.

steps.name: tail
steps.text_tex: Evaluate a tail probability of the form 1 minus a sum of binomial terms for X greater than or equal to 17 (one end error allowed). The official scheme requires the complementary form 1 minus a sum.
steps.note: MS: M1 Allow one end error. Must have 1 minus a sum of binomial terms.

steps.name: comp
steps.text_tex: Compare 0.0706 with 0.05. A valid comparison is required.
steps.note: MS: M1 Compare with 0.05. Valid comparison needed.

steps.name: conc
steps.text_tex: Conclude that there is no evidence that the percentage is less than 92%, in context, with no contradictions. (Official alternative after the first two B marks: a continuity-corrected normal comparison of 1.566 with 1.645, or 1.978 without a continuity correction, leading to a corresponding conclusion and SC2 after the B marks.)
steps.note: MS: A1FT OE. No evidence that percentage less than 92%. No contradictions. Normal-approximation alternative as in the official guidance.

title: One-tailed test of P(throwing a six)=1/6, using a normal approximation

source.note: Stem verbatim from the QP PDF (the printed fractions 1/6 were flattened by pdftotext as 16; they were checked on the rendered page). Steps and marks from the official MS PDF. The item is a one-tailed test at the 10% level and does not ask for Type I/II errors. Fully manual, steps only, because the hypotheses and the conclusion are verbal. The standardised value z=-1.486 was independently confirmed from N(100/3, 250/9) with a continuity correction.

stem: A six-sided die shows a six on 25 throws out of 200 throws. Test at the 10% significance level the null hypothesis: \(\mathrm{P}(\text{throwing a six})=\dfrac{1}{6}\), against the alternative hypothesis: \(\mathrm{P}(\text{throwing a six})\lt \dfrac{1}{6}\).

steps.name: approx
steps.text_tex: Use the normal approximation \(\mathrm{B}(200,\dfrac{1}{6})\to\mathrm{N}(\dfrac{100}{3},\dfrac{250}{9})\), seen or implied.
steps.note: MS: B1 B(200, 1/6) to N(100/3, 250/9), seen or implied.

steps.name: zform
steps.text_tex: Standardise with a continuity correction, for example \((25.5-100/3)/\sqrt{250/9}\). A wrong continuity correction, or none, is allowed at this mark.
steps.note: MS: M1 allow with wrong or no cc.

steps.name: zval
steps.text_tex: Obtain z = -1.486. Alternative correct methods are accepted.
steps.note: MS: A1 = -1.486. Accept alternative correct methods.

steps.name: comp
steps.text_tex: Compare 1.486 with 1.282, or compare the corresponding probability with 0.1.
steps.note: MS: M1 comp 1.486 with 1.282, or comp with 0.1.

steps.name: conc
steps.text_tex: Give evidence to reject H0, in context and without contradictions: there is some evidence that p < 1/6, or it is likely that p < 1/6.
steps.note: MS: A1 ft. Evidence to reject H0. There is some evidence that p < 1/6, or e.g. it is likely that p < 1/6, oe. No contradictions.
